    // The lower Tukey fence: LowerQuartile - 1.5 * IQR. Values below it are
    // candidate outliers under the standard 1.5-IQR rule.
    LowerFence(self: FiveNumberSummary): Number
        => self.LowerQuartile - Number.TukeyFenceMultiplier * self.InterquartileRange;

    // The upper Tukey fence: UpperQuartile + 1.5 * IQR.
    UpperFence(self: FiveNumberSummary): Number
        => self.UpperQuartile + Number.TukeyFenceMultiplier * self.InterquartileRange;

    // The span covered by the whiskers: UpperWhisker - LowerWhisker.
    WhiskerRange(self: BoxPlotStatistics): Number
        => self.UpperWhisker - self.LowerWhisker;

    // The number of data values lying beyond the whiskers.
    OutlierCount(self: BoxPlotStatistics): Integer
        => self.Outliers.Count;

    // True when no value lies beyond the whiskers.
    HasNoOutliers(self: BoxPlotStatistics): Boolean
        => self.Outliers.Count == 0;

    //==
    // # Deliberate gaps
    //
    // TODO(content): the ESTIMATORS are not implemented here. Computing a
    // SummaryStatistics, FiveNumberSummary, Quantiles or BoxPlotStatistics from
    // an Array<Number> needs a sort (this vocabulary declares none) and a choice
    // among the nine standard quantile-interpolation conventions; building a
    // Histogram from a sample needs the accumulation surface the affine builders
    // now supply (`List.Freeze` in primitives.plato) plus a binning convention.
    // Spearman and Kendall correlation need ranking, i.e. a
    // sort. MovingAverage and OutlierDetection are sum types describing a rule,
    // and applying a rule to a series again needs the accumulation surface.
    // These are gaps of missing infrastructure, not of missing formulas.

    //==
    // # Covariance, correlation, and fit bodies
    //
    // The bivariate half of the statistics domain (`statistics.types.plato`):
    // the trace, determinant and implied
    // Pearson correlation of a Covariance2D, the closed-form evaluation of a fitted
    // line or polynomial, and the derived readings of a CorrelationCoefficient. As
    // in the section above, only relations that follow from the field
    // definitions by identity appear here — the estimators that would *produce*
    // these records need a sorting surface this vocabulary does not declare.

    //==
    // # Covariance
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covariance_matrix

    // The trace of the 2x2 covariance: the total variance Xx + Yy.
    TotalVariance(self: Covariance2D): Number
        => self.Xx + self.Yy;

    // The determinant of the 2x2 covariance: Xx*Yy - Xy^2. Non-negative for any
    // genuine covariance; zero when the sample is perfectly collinear.
    Determinant(self: Covariance2D): Number
        => self.Xx * self.Yy - self.Xy.Square;

    // The Pearson correlation implied by the covariance:
    // Xy / sqrt(Xx * Yy), in [-1, 1]. Precondition: both variances positive.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearson_correlation_coefficient
    PearsonCorrelation(self: Covariance2D): Number
        => self.Xy / (self.Xx * self.Yy).Sqrt;

    // The standard deviation of x: the square root of its variance.
    StandardDeviationX(self: Covariance2D): Number
        => self.Xx.Sqrt;

    // The standard deviation of y: the square root of its variance.
    StandardDeviationY(self: Covariance2D): Number
        => self.Yy.Sqrt;

    //==
    // # Fits
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simple_linear_regression
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coefficient_of_determination

    // The fitted value at x: Slope * x + Intercept.
    Predict(self: LinearFit, x: Number): Number
        => self.Slope * x + self.Intercept;

    // The x at which the fitted line crosses zero: -Intercept / Slope.
    // Precondition: Slope is non-zero.
    RootOfFit(self: LinearFit): Number
        => -self.Intercept / self.Slope;

    // The residual of an observation: the observed y minus the fitted value.
    Residual(self: LinearFit, x: Number, y: Number): Number
        => y - self.Predict(x);

    // The magnitude of the correlation implied by the fit: sqrt(R^2). The sign
    // of the correlation is the sign of the Slope, which this does not apply.
    CorrelationMagnitude(self: LinearFit): Number
        => self.RSquared.Sqrt;

    // The degree of the fitted polynomial: the coefficient count minus one.
    Degree(self: PolynomialFit): Integer
        => self.Coefficients.Count - 1;

    // The fitted value at x, by Horner evaluation of the ASCENDING-power
    // coefficient array (Coefficients[k] multiplies x^k).
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horner%27s_method
    Predict(self: PolynomialFit, x: Number): Number
        => self.Coefficients.Count.Range
            .Map(k => self.Coefficients[k] * x.Pow(k.ToNumber))
            .Reduce(0.0, (total, term) => total + term);

    //==
    // # CorrelationCoefficient
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Correlation

    // The coefficient of determination for a correlation: the square of the
    // coefficient, in [0, 1].
    RSquared(self: CorrelationCoefficient): Number
        => self.Value.Square;

    // The strength of association, ignoring direction: the absolute value of
    // the coefficient, in [0, 1].
    Strength(self: CorrelationCoefficient): Number
        => self.Value.Abs;

    // True when the two variables move in opposite directions.
    IsNegative(self: CorrelationCoefficient): Boolean
        => self.Value < 0.0;
}
